messages:
Emily S: Hey team — PearlPay POC kicks off Mon. They sent traffic profile: ~8k peak requests/min (chat), typical input ~30 tokens, output ~120 tokens. Hard constraint: p95 latency target <250ms for interactive flows. They asked for a recommended reserved GPU plan + autoscale + burst credit guidance. cc @Raj P @Maya L

Raj P: quick clarifying q's — is 8k RPM a sustained steady-state or short spikes? are requests evenly distributed across a 60s window or spiky (eg, cron-driven)? also which model do they want to serve for the POC? streaming or non-streaming?

Emily S: They said peaks are bursty (campaign windows) — baseline ~4k RPM with spikes up to 8k for 3–10m. Want to test redwood/fastchat-13b (fp16) with streaming.

Maya L: rough back-of-envelope: 8k RPM = ~133 RPS. With 120 output tokens avg => ~16k tokens/s. If one A100-style GPU can handle ~3.5k tok/s for 13B fp16 under our optimized kernel (varies by seq len/beam), we need ~5 GPUs sustained to hit token throughput, but latency targets push us to keep concurrency lower -> recommend reserved pool + prewarm + burst.

Maya L: recommendation for POC (minimal risk):
- Reserved baseline: 6 GPUs (dedicated pool) to cover steady + safety.
- Prewarm / headroom: 2 GPUs hot but not always billed as committed (reserved warm slots) to absorb short spikes.
- Burst credits / autoscale: allow autoscale up to +4 GPUs for 10min windows (total cap 12) using burst credits.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to quantized 7B variant if p95 > 250ms after scaled burst (keeps UX acceptable).

Ken R: pricing implications: recommend we present two options to PearlPay — (A) 6-GPU committed monthly + burst block priced as X credits; (B) smaller commit (4 GPUs) + higher burst allowance. Option A gives them predictable unit cost and lower effective per-token price. I'll draft numbers once we confirm target commitment length.

Ava C: security note from PearlPay: they want a short answers doc on data isolation and logging for the POC. If we run Dedicated, we can provide per-tenant audit logs and KMS-integration notes. I'll pair with Maya to add a one-pager for the customer.

Raj P: ops/runbook items for the POC:
- Autoscale policy: start scale-up at p95 latency > 180ms for 30s window; scale in only after p95 < 150ms for 2m. Use step scaling: +1 GPU per 30s up to burst cap.
- Prewarm logic: maintain 2 always-warm instances with KV cache warmed for common prefixes (saves ~40–60ms on first token).
- Routing: prefer AZ-affine routing; enable cross-AZ fallback only if local capacity exhausted.

Raj P: simple health checks to add to runbook (snippet):
- /health model -> 200 if model loaded
- /metrics latency.p95, tokens/s, gpu_utilization
- alert if gpu_utilization > 90% for 60s AND latency.p95 > 200ms

Emily S: perfect. Can you also add a short failure-mode playbook? PearlPay wants to know how we keep UX online if GPUs are exhausted.

Maya L: failure-mode checklist (short):
1) Automatic model fallback to quantized 7B variant for non-critical paths.
2) Enable prefix/KV cache to reduce repeated compute.
3) Route low-priority traffic to a best-effort pool (no SLA).
4) Notify CS + oncall; if outage >5m, trigger emergency burst allocation and offer credit backfill.

Ken R: I'll update the commercial options and include burst credit examples. Emily — want me to run a quick cost calc for 30/60/90 day commit?

Emily S: yes please, 60-day and 12-month numbers. Also please keep the POC pricing flexible for a small added premium to allow burst credits.

deploy-bot: deployment started: reserved-pool-pearlpay v1.3 -> staging (CI #4521) :rocket:

Raj P: I'll draft the autoscale config (yaml) and paste here once ready.

Emily S: amazing — can we have the one-pager + pricing options by EOD Friday? I’ll present to PearlPay on Monday. :thumbsup:

Maya L: yep — I’ll do the runbook + fallback playbook. Raj will do the autoscale YAML. Ken will do commercial options. Ava will do security Q answers. We’ll hand a consolidated packet to Emily by Fri EOD.

Ken R: acked.

Ava C: will reach out to PearlPay about the security questionnaire questions we still need (encryption at rest, key management, retention).

Emily S: thanks all — high-level deliverables: 1) sizing + reserved plan, 2) autoscale/runbook + YAML, 3) pricing options, 4) security one-pager. Pulling into a single doc for the customer.

Maya L: will add notes about observability (per-route token breakdown) so PearlPay can validate cost during the POC.

Emily S: great — closing this thread when docs are in.
